user.title: Set up EPSNET

data.name: Name

data_description.scan_interval: Pause after each full read of the PLC's values. Default 500; 0 starts the next read immediately. The fast lane for buttons is under Configure once set up.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure EPSNET connection

source_plc_busy.title: Choose the variable map source
source_plc_busy.description:
Discover the published-variable map straight from the PLC (recommended), or upload an exported .pub file.

⚠️ The PLC is busy (its exclusive session is held, e.g. by FoxTool). Close other tools and try again.

source_cannot_connect.title: Choose the variable map source
source_cannot_connect.description:
Discover the published-variable map straight from the PLC (recommended), or upload an exported .pub file.

⚠️ Could not reach the PLC. Check the host and ports, then try again — or upload a .pub file instead.

source_no_map.title: Choose the variable map source
source_no_map.description:
Discover the published-variable map straight from the PLC (recommended), or upload an exported .pub file.

⚠️ The PLC holds no published-variable map (no .pub was stored in it — e.g. a program loaded from Mosaic). Upload the .pub file from your project instead; in Mosaic, enable it under Project manager → Sw → Export files → Assembler (.pub) and rebuild.

init.title: EPSNET
init.description:
Source: {source} · PLC: {ident} · {points} points · CRC {crc}

**Re-import the variable map** after changing the PLC program, so Home Assistant reads and switches the right variables. Entities keep their IDs.
- **From the PLC** reads the map stored in the PLC together with the program.
- **From a file** uploads the `.pub` exported with the program. Use it when the PLC stores no map, or an old one.

**Polling intervals** set how often values are read from the PLC.

menu_options.reimport_plc: Re-import the variable map from the PLC
menu_options.reimport_file: Re-import the variable map from a file (.pub)

settings.title: Polling intervals
settings.description: How often Home Assistant reads values from the PLC. Shorter intervals give faster updates but more network traffic and load on the PLC. Saving reloads the integration.

data.fast_scan_interval: Fast lane for buttons and motion sensors (milliseconds)

data_description.scan_interval: Each cycle reads every value the integration uses (a few hundred values take about half a second), then waits this long before the next one. Default 500; 0 starts the next read immediately.
data_description.fast_scan_interval: Reads only the on/off inputs (wall buttons, motion sensors, contacts) on their own short cycle, so a quick button press isn't missed between full reads. 0 = off; 100 is recommended (about 10 small requests per second).

reimport_file.title: Re-import from a file
reimport_file.description: Upload the `.pub` / `.piz` / `.zip` exported with the program that is running in the PLC now. The PLC's modules are still scanned live to match the map to them. If the file can't be used, the current map is kept.

map_changed.title: EPSNET PLC program changed
map_changed.description: The PLC's published-variable map changed since the last import (CRC {old_crc} → {new_crc}, {points} points). The new map has been applied. Review your entities and automations in case variable addresses moved.

unsupported_modules.title: EPSNET: PLC modules not supported yet
unsupported_modules.description: {count} module(s) on the PLC bus are not supported yet ({codes}), so they have no entities. To help add them, open the EPSNET integration, choose ⋮ → Download diagnostics and attach the file to an issue at {issue_url}. The file contains your PLC variable names; rename them in the file if you prefer.

no_variable_map.title: EPSNET: no PLC variable map
no_variable_map.description: This entry has no published-variable map, so its {count} module(s) are listed without entities: without the map it is unknown where their data sits and how to switch them. Open the integration, choose Configure → Re-import the variable map from the PLC, or delete and re-add the integration and upload the program's .pub file.
